title: Components of the endomembrane system
body: The endomembrane system is a group of membrane-bound organelles and subcellular components that work together to modify, package, and transport polysaccharides, lipids, and proteins.
ced_evidence: EK 2.1.A.2: "endoplasmic reticulum (ER), Golgi complex, lysosomes, vacuoles and transport vesicles, the nuclear envelope, and the plasma membrane"

title: Cell size and surface area-to-volume ratio
body: As cells increase in volume, the surface area-to-volume ratio decreases and the demand for internal resources increases, so smaller cells typically have a higher SA:V and exchange materials with the environment more efficiently.
ced_evidence: EK 2.2.A.2.i-ii: "As cells increase in volume, the surface area-to-volume ratio decreases and the demand for internal resources increases."

title: Membrane folds compensate for low SA:V
body: More complex cellular structures, such as membrane folds, are necessary to adequately exchange materials with the environment.
ced_evidence: EK 2.2.A.2.iii: "More complex cellular structures (e.g., membrane folds) are necessary to adequately exchange materials with the environment."

title: Cell wall
body: In Bacteria, Archaea, Fungi, and plants, the cell wall provides a structural boundary, a permeability barrier for some substances, and protection from osmotic lysis.
ced_evidence: EK 2.4.B.1: "provide a structural boundary as well as a permeability barrier for some substances ... and protection from osmotic lysis"

title: Aquaporin
body: Aquaporins are membrane proteins that transport large quantities of water across membranes.
ced_evidence: EK 2.6.A.3: "Aquaporins transport large quantities of water across membranes."

title: Facilitated diffusion
body: Facilitated diffusion uses transport or channel proteins to move charged ions and large polar molecules across the membrane down their concentration gradient with no energy input.
ced_evidence: EK 2.6.A.1-2: "requires transport or channel proteins"; "movement of large polar molecules through membranes with no energy input"

title: Tonicity of the external environment
body: An external environment can be hypotonic, hypertonic, or isotonic to the internal environment of cells, and water moves by osmosis from regions of high water potential to regions of low water potential.
ced_evidence: EK 2.7.A.1: "External environments can be hypotonic, hypertonic, or isotonic to internal environments of cells."

title: Ions need channel proteins; ion movement can polarize membranes
body: Charged ions such as Na+ and K+ require channel proteins to cross the membrane, and the movement of ions across the membrane can polarize the membrane.
ced_evidence: EK 2.6.A.1.i-ii: "Membranes may become polarized by the movement of ions across the membrane"; "Charged ions, including Na+ (sodium) and K+ (potassium), require channel proteins"
